- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:257-270 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `_GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS` (`{0,8}` quantifier) matches at most eight Git global options, so a verdict like `git -c a=b` repeated nine times followed by `fetch origin main` is not classified as `git_remote_op`, and no other pattern catches it (`origin main` without a slash does not trip `origin_ref`).
  WHY: `validate --sandbox-check` / `_check_sandbox_instructions` accepts the verdict, so `unblock_judge.sh` never re-asks and the network-less implementer is told to fetch, which is the fun-token-multi-chain#639 failure. All four reviewers rated it SEVERITY: NIT, mapped here to low. Reviewers note it is unlikely and no worse than pre-PR behaviour, and the gemini reviewer notes the sandbox still blocks it at execution time. The anthropic reviewer adds that the cap cannot simply be raised, because `_GIT_OPT_VALUE` (line 256) has overlapping alternatives (`"[^"\n]*"` vs `\S+`), so failed matches cost about 2^n. minimax_minimax-m3 explicitly disputed raising this as a finding, saying the bound is the deliberate ReDoS fix.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:lines 257-261, `_GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS` ending in `)){0,8}`, used by `git_remote_op` at lines 269-270 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The global-option skip is capped at eight tokens. A remote command with 9 or more global options (for example, nine `-c a=b` then `fetch origin main`) is not matched, `origin main` does not trip `origin_ref`, and `_check_sandbox_instructions` (lines 896-902) accepts the verdict.
  WHY: `validate --sandbox-check` succeeds and `unblock_judge.sh` sets `validate_ok=true` and never re-asks, so the fix-up tells the network-less implementer to fetch (fun-token-multi-chain#639). This is a heuristic gap, not an exploitable boundary; the impact equals pre-PR behaviour and no test pins the cap. The cap cannot be raised to `*` or `{0,32}` because `_GIT_OPT_VALUE` (line 256) overlaps: a quoted `"a"` matches both `"[^"\n]*"` and `\S+`, so failed matches cost about 2^n and the ReDoS would return. The comment at lines 253-255 ("the alternatives are disjoint") is untrue for the value sub-pattern.
- HARDENING: scripts/unblock_ledger.py line 256, `_GIT_OPT_VALUE`
  ISSUE: The unquoted alternative `\S+` also matches quoted tokens, so the alternatives are not disjoint.
  FIX: Change it to `[^\s"'][^\s]*`, then raise the cap to `{0,32}` (or `*`). Add a test with nine `-c a=b` options then `fetch` (expect `sandbox_incompatible:git_remote_op`), and add 30 quoted `-c "a"` options then `status` to the timing test. About 1-2 regex lines and 6 test lines.
- HARDENING: scripts/unblock_ledger.py lines 253-255, comment
  ISSUE: The comment claims disjoint alternatives, but the value sub-pattern overlaps.
  FIX: Correct the comment or make it true with the change above (1 line).
- TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE. The CLAUDE.md section 19 "Implements #N" bullet is deliberately deferred and recorded as IMPLEMENTS_MARKER_CLAUDE_MD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP in agents.d/7765-implements-marker.md.
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:Lines 257-261 (_GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: _GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS limits git global options to a maximum of 8, so commands with 9 or more global options bypass git_remote_op detection.
  WHY: The regex requires the subcommand (for example, fetch) to come right after at most 8 option tokens. This bypasses the sandbox-check optimization, but the networkless sandbox still blocks the command at execution time.

It also says the precondition is unlikely, since `ROUND2_639` has no such options.
- NOTE: The reviewer says the disjointness claims hold for the option alternatives (Alt 1 vs Alt 4 lookahead, and Alt 2 vs Alt 3 names). It hand-traced the listed commands, which all match `git_remote_op`.
- NOTE: The check runs on text already truncated by `_clean_text` (`MAX_TEXT = 1200`, line 818; `scripts/unblock_ledger.py:1018-1022`). The fix-up sees the same truncated text, so nothing is lost.
